mainTopic: אביי's ברייתא challenge to רב יוסף, רבא's rereading of it, and a question on רבי's view
overview: Earlier, רב יוסף explained that the משנה about mixed-up offerings must be talking about women's קרבנות. The reason is that men's offerings need סמיכה. אביי challenges him from a ברייתא about a קרבן יחיד mixed with a קרבן יחיד or with a קרבן ציבור. In that ברייתא each animal still gets its own מתנות, and since יחיד is listed next to ציבור, the יחיד must belong to men too. רבא answers by questioning the ברייתא: why should it matter whether the animals were alive or slaughtered? He rereads it as being only about slaughtered animals. If each animal's blood is in its own cup, the כהן gives from each one. If the blood is mixed together, four מתנות for all of them are enough, and after the fact even one. So the ברייתא says nothing about live animals and does not argue against רב יוסף. The גמרא then turns to רבי's view in the same ברייתא, that a shared מתנה must hold enough blood for each offering. It begins to question whether רבי really holds this, quoting another ברייתא in which רבי speaks according to רבי אליעזר; that quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי quotes a ברייתא about mixed individual and communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins his challenge to רב יוסף by quoting a ברייתא. It says that mixed offerings of a יחיד and a ציבור each get four מתנות, and after the fact one מתנה from each, or four for all together, is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: If an individual's offering got mixed with another individual's offering, or a communal offering with another communal offering, or an individual's offering with a communal offering, the כהן puts four placements of blood from each one. If he put one placement from each, he has fulfilled his duty. If he put four placements for all of them together, he has also fulfilled his duty.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens an attack on רב יוסף by quoting a ברייתא. The actual point of the attack comes in step 4, so for now the גמרא is setting up the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats mixed animals as still usable, with each one brought for its owner. It lists three cases: יחיד with יחיד, ציבור with ציבור, and יחיד with ציבור. The best way is four מתנות from each animal, but one מתנה from each, or four for all together, also works after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought by a single person
An offering brought on behalf of the whole community
Got mixed up
Placements of blood on the מזבח
He has fulfilled his obligation (at least after the fact)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the problem with רב יוסף in these lines yet. The ברייתא is only being quoted now; the challenge is spelled out in step 4.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, who said our משנה is talking about women's offerings.

phrases.english: An individual's offering that got mixed with another individual's offering,
and a communal offering that got mixed with another communal offering,

phrases.aramaic: וְקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד וְקׇרְבַּן צִיבּוּר שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ זֶה בָּזֶה –
phrases.english: and an individual's offering and a communal offering that got mixed with each other —

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן אַרְבַּע מַתָּנוֹת מִכׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: he places four placements of blood from each and every one.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נָתַן מַתָּנָה מִכׇּל אֶחָד – יָצָא,
phrases.english: And if he placed one placement from each one, he has fulfilled his duty,
and if he placed four for all of them together, he has fulfilled his duty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens אביי's challenge to רב יוסף's statement on the previous section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the משנה must be about women's offerings, since men's mixed offerings would have a problem with סמיכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets mixed offerings of a יחיד be brought, and step 4 will show that the יחיד here means men.

steps.title: The ברייתא limits its rule to animals mixed while alive
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that giving separate מתנות from each animal applies only when the animals were mixed while still alive. If they were mixed after שחיטה, four מתנות for all of them together is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When they got mixed while alive. But if they got mixed after being slaughtered, he places four placements from all of them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is still being quoted. It now explains when the first rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If live animals got mixed, each one is slaughtered on its own, so the כהן has separate blood to give from each. If the animals were already slaughtered and their blood got mixed, there is no way to separate it. So one set of four מתנות covers everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: "In what case is this said?" — a phrase that limits a rule
Alive (still living animals)
Already slaughtered

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
When they got mixed while alive,
but if they got mixed after being slaughtered —
phrases.notes: He means their blood got mixed together in one bowl.

phrases.english: he places four placements from all of them together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא and limits its first rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separate מתנות from each animal apply only when the animals were mixed while alive. If the blood got mixed after שחיטה, four מתנות for all of them together is the way to do it.

steps.title: One placement works after the fact, and רבי adds a condition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that even one מתנה for all of them works after the fact. רבי disagrees and says it depends on whether that blood is enough for each offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he placed one placement for all of them, he has fulfilled his duty. רבי says: We look at the placement. If it contains enough blood for this one and enough for that one, it is valid. If not, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes. It gives the minimum that works after the fact, and then רבי disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offerings whose blood goes on the outer מזבח need only one מתנה after the fact. So the תנא קמא says one placement of the mixed blood covers all of them. רבי adds a condition: that one placement must hold enough blood to count as a placement for each offering, or it does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: We look at / we check
Enough for this one and enough for that one
Valid
Disqualified

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נָתַן מַתָּנָה אַחַת מִכּוּלָּן – יָצָא.
phrases.english: And if he placed one placement for all of them, he has fulfilled his duty.
Rabbi says: We look at the placement;

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ כְּדֵי לָזֶה וּכְדֵי לָזֶה – כְּשֵׁרָה,
phrases.english: if it has enough blood for this one and enough for that one, it is valid,
and if not, it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא with the after-the-fact minimum and רבי's disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, one מתנה for all the mixed offerings works after the fact. רבי says it works only if that blood is enough for each offering.

steps.title: The individual offering is like the communal one, so it belongs to men
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the challenge. The ברייתא puts יחיד right next to ציבור, and a ציבור offering belongs to men. So the יחיד in the ברייתא also means men, and still the mixed animals may be brought. That goes against רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא teaches the individual's offering next to the communal offering, so they are alike. Just as a communal offering belongs to men, so too the individual's offering here belongs to men.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא spells out why the ברייתא is a problem for רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said mixed offerings can be brought only if they belong to women, because men need סמיכה. But the ברייתא lists יחיד together with ציבור, which shows they are the same kind of case. Since a ציבור offering certainly belongs to men, the יחיד offering here belongs to men too, and the ברייתא still allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (the ברייתא says)
Similar to, alike
Men

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's challenge: the ברייתא puts יחיד next to ציבור, so the יחיד offering is a man's offering just like the ציבור one. Even so, the mixed animals are brought, which goes against רב יוסף's claim that this works only for women's offerings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This raises the question of whether the need for סמיכה stops mixed-up men's offerings from being brought. That is the key point in רב יוסף's reading of the משנה.

phrases.english: It teaches the individual's offering together with the communal offering, so they are alike —
just as a communal offering belongs to men,
so too the individual's offering belongs to men.
phrases.notes: Men's offerings need סמיכה, so this is exactly the case רב יוסף said could not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in steps 1–3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the משנה must be about women's offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the ברייתא lists יחיד next to ציבור, the יחיד offering belongs to men. Yet the mixed animals are still brought, so סמיכה does not block it, and רב יוסף has no need to say the case is about women.

steps.title: רבא questions whether the ברייתא makes sense as read
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the ברייתא's line that separate מתנות apply only to animals mixed while alive, not after שחיטה. Why should alive versus slaughtered make any difference?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Can you really understand the ברייתא this way? Is it well-worded as it stands? It says the rule of separate מתנות applies when the animals got mixed alive, but not when they got mixed after שחיטה. What difference does it make whether they were alive or slaughtered?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the ברייתא as אביי read it. He says the line between live and slaughtered animals makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after שחיטה, each animal's blood could still be sitting in its own cup. Then the כהן could still give separate מתנות from each one, exactly as with live animals. So 'alive versus slaughtered' cannot be the real dividing line, and רבא is getting ready to reread the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Well-put, worded correctly as it stands
Alive, meaning the animals got mixed before שחיטה
Slaughtered, meaning mixed after שחיטה
What difference is it to me? Used to say two cases should be the same

phrases.english: Rava said: And can you understand it this way?
Is this ברייתא well-put as it stands?!
For it teaches: In what case are these words said?
When they were mixed while alive,
but if they were mixed after being slaughtered, it does not apply.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי חַיִּים מָה לִי שְׁחוּטִין?
phrases.english: What difference is it to me whether they are alive or slaughtered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא responds to אביי's challenge by first questioning the ברייתא that אביי relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line between animals mixed alive and animals mixed after שחיטה, as אביי read it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Alive versus slaughtered should not matter, because slaughtered animals whose blood sits in separate cups can also get separate מתנות.

steps.title: רבא rereads the ברייתא as about blood in cups
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא only speaks about slaughtered animals. If the blood is still in separate cups (like live animals), you give from each. If the blood was poured together, four מתנות for all of them is enough, and after the fact even one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the ברייתא means. When does the rule of separate מתנות apply? When slaughtered animals got mixed but are still 'like live ones,' because each animal's blood is in its own cup. But when the blood itself is mixed together, the כהן gives four מתנות for all of them. And if he gave just one מתנה for all, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new reading of the ברייתא that fixes the problem he raised. On his reading, the ברייתא only deals with blood after שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new reading, both cases involve animals that were already slaughtered. 'Like live ones' means each animal's blood is still in its own cup, and בּוֹלֵל means the blood was mixed together. So the ברייתא never talks about live animals getting mixed, cannot prove anything against רב יוסף, and אביי's challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it means. Introduces a new reading of a source
Similar to live animals, meaning each animal's blood is still kept apart
Cups or vessels holding the blood
Mixed together, meaning the blood was poured into one cup
He has fulfilled his obligation, it counts after the fact

steps.whatToRemember: רבא reads the ברייתא as about blood only: separate cups means separate מתנות, and mixed blood means four for all (one after the fact). So it proves nothing about live animals and does not argue against רב יוסף.
steps.confusionAlert: In רבא's reading, every animal in the ברייתא is already slaughtered. 'Like live ones' does not mean the animals are alive. It only means each animal's blood is still kept in its own cup, as opposed to בּוֹלֵל, where the blood is mixed together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading removes the source אביי used against רב יוסף, so רב יוסף's position survives.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
In what case are these words said?
When slaughtered animals got mixed in a way similar to live ones,
in separate cups;
but where the blood is mixed together,
he gives four placements for all of them.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נָתַן מַתָּנָה אַחַת לְכוּלָּן – יָצָא.
phrases.english: And if he gave one placement for all of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty רבא himself raised in step 5 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא contrasts live animals that got mixed with slaughtered ones, so it supports bringing mixed live animals of a יחיד and a ציבור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא deals only with slaughtered animals: blood in separate cups versus blood mixed together. So it says nothing about live animals and cannot challenge רב יוסף.

steps.title: The ברייתא quotes רבי's view on measuring the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רבי's opinion from the ברייתא. A single מתנה works only if it has enough blood for each offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: We look at the מתנה. If it has enough blood for this offering and enough for that one, it is valid. If not, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי's line in the ברייתא. It is setting up a question about this opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that a shared מתנה counts only if there is enough blood in it for each offering on its own. This sets the stage for the next step, which asks whether רבי really holds that there is a required amount for each part of a mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: We look at, we check
Enough, the needed amount
Valid
Invalid, disqualified

phrases.english: Rabbi says: We look at the placement;

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ כְּדֵי לָזֶה וּכְדֵי לָזֶה – כְּשֵׁרָה,
phrases.english: if there is enough in it for this one and enough for that one, it is valid,
and if not, it is invalid.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מימרא as part of the ברייתא's continuation
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבא's rereading of the ברייתא to רבי's opinion at the end of that same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, one מתנה for mixed offerings is valid only if it holds enough blood for each offering.

steps.title: Does רבי really hold this view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי really holds that each offering needs its own amount of blood. It starts to quote a different ברייתא in which רבי speaks according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי really hold this reasoning? Isn't it taught in a ברייתא: רבי said, according to the words of רבי אליעזר...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רבי's view in step 7 by bringing another ברייתא. The quote is only starting here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ' signal that רבי seems to say something else elsewhere. The other ברייתא opens with רבי explaining רבי אליעזר's position. Its content, which will show the contradiction, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really hold? Introduces a contradiction from another source
Line of reasoning, view
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? Brings a source that seems to contradict

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי הַאי סְבָרָא?!
phrases.english: And does Rabbi really hold this reasoning?!
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi said:
According to the words of Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: The quote stops in the middle here. The rest of what רבי says comes at the start of the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי הַאי סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of רבי that was just quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's view that each offering needs enough blood in a shared מתנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא, where רבי speaks according to רבי אליעזר, seems to show רבי does not hold this reasoning. The details come in the continuation.
